chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt. He said: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him):
What do you say regarding the Quran? He said: It is the word of God. Do not go beyond it, and do not seek guidance in other than it, or you will be misguided.

key_terms.الْهُدَى: Guidance (al-huda) — divine direction toward truth and righteousness
key_terms.فَتَضِلُّوا: Or you will be misguided (tadillu) — the consequence of abandoning the Quran as one's sole guide
key_terms.كَلَامُ اللَّهِ: The speech/word of God — a theological designation for the Quran asserting its divine origin
key_terms.لَا تَتَجَاوَزُوهُ: Do not go beyond it — an injunction against surpassing the limits set by scripture

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the nature of the Quran and seeking guidance?
ai.summary: In this hadith, al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt asks Imam al-Rida (AS) directly about the nature of the Quran, and the Imam replies with a terse but profound creedal statement: the Quran is the speech of God, and all guidance must be sought within it alone. This narration was likely transmitted in a context where various heterodox positions about the createdness or nature of the Quran were circulating, and the Imam's brief declaration served as a clear doctrinal anchor. The warning against seeking guidance outside the Quran reflects the Shia theological insistence on the Quran as the supreme and unalterable source of divine guidance.
